rules.rationale: Dense N/O centers donate and accept hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable term in aqueous hydration free energy.
Broader polar tier (91 items); partial hydrogen-bonding capacity still offsets the cavity-formation penalty in water.
Pure hydrocarbons offer neither hydrogen bonding nor polarizable substituents, so cavity cost stays uncompensated.
Heavily halogenated solutes resemble fluorocarbons: large apolar surface, weak water interaction, unfavorable hydration.

skills.hypothesis: Hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding capacity and penalizes apolar or perhalogenated surfaces, ignoring low-confidence size transfer. Fails if the score instead rewards small apolar solutes or if thin hetero_high/halogen_high bins are unrepresentative.

rules.rationale: Explicit source value prior positive for smiles_short; small solutes pay a low cavity-formation cost in water.
Largest-magnitude source prior (-11.46, confidence 0.47) for smiles_long; bulky solutes expose broad hydrophobic surface.
Counter-hypothesis: ESOL ring penalty reflects crystal packing, absent here; aromatic rings accept weak water interactions.
Rotatable-bond role transfers to branching (weight 0.758); bulky branched aliphatics maximize apolar surface area.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the explicit ESOL size priors while reversing the uncertain ring relation and keeping branching negative. Fails if hydration is polarity-driven rather than size-driven, since source role confidences are only 0.16-0.41.

state.lesson: Source ESOL evidence is size- and ring-dominated with low confidence (0.16-0.41) and mixes lattice terms absent from hydration free energy, so a mechanism-first polarity prior over well-populated bins remains the safer deployment, with decaying semantic mass letting revealed target data override it.
